# API Token Authentication

Use an API token for token-based automation credentials.

## Step 1: Create Credentials

Create the token in the F5 XC Console by following [Generate API Tokens for My
Credentials](https://flatrender.tora.reviews/docs-v2/administration/how-tos/user-mgmt/Credentials#generate-api-tokens-for-my-credentials).

## Step 2: Set Environment Variables

Store the token in a CI/CD secret manager and inject it as
`F5XCProvider_API_TOKEN` at runtime.

```sh
export F5XCProvider_URL="https://<tenant>.console.ves.volterra.io/api"
export F5XCProvider_API_TOKEN="<api-token>"
```

The provider block can then omit credentials:

```terraform
provider "f5xc" {}
```

Alternatively, configure the token with a sensitive Terraform variable:

```terraform
variable "f5xc_api_token" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

provider "f5xc" {
  url       = "https://<tenant>.console.ves.volterra.io/api"
  api_token = var.f5xc_api_token
}
```

## Step 3: Test Namespace Creation

Create a namespace to verify the provider can authenticate to F5 XC:

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    f5xc = {
      source = "F5Networks/f5xc"
    }
  }
}

resource "f5xc_namespace" "authentication_test" {
  name        = "terraform-auth-test"
  description = "Created to verify API token authentication."
}
```

Do not commit API tokens to Terraform configuration. Terraform marks
`api_token` sensitive in CLI output, but sensitive values can still be stored
in state. Use an encrypted, access-controlled remote backend.

Return to the [authentication overview](authentication.md).
